story_text:
Need to scan a small precision part, a reflective metal component, and a large workpiece?
Meet MIRACO 2. This portable all-in-one 3D scanner brings blue laser scanning, infrared structured light, and photogrammetric metrology into one flexible workflow. Scan and review results directly on its touchscreen, or connect to a PC when your project calls for faster capture and more processing power.
Go from the smallest details to the bigger picture without changing scanners.
## Referral Program
## The Reviews Are In
"The MIRACO 2 is really all you need, in 1 unit! You dont need to have it hooked up to a computer so in reality you can bring it with you in case you need to scan something away from home or on a trip. The large touch screen makes it really easy to use. I have used it to reverse engineer car parts. My only problem is that it has so many features that I havent had time to try them all yet."
—— Critical
"I've been really impressed with the Miraco 2. The ease of use and scanning speed are probably what stood out to me the most, especially considering the level of detail it captures. Even in standalone mode, without being connected to a computer, the results are impressive."
—— Mike Martin
“The MIRACO is my favorite scanner for one simple reason: portability and it's completely standalone. [...] Every time I was like, it's too bad, every time there is a very strong daylight, I'm in trouble. And now the MIRACO 2 fixed that major issue that I had.”
—— Julien Roméo
“What I liked most about the MIRACO 2 was being able to scan without bringing a laptop. I can check the results on the built-in screen and start cleaning up the scan right on the device. With six scanning modes and blue laser lines that are new to the MIRACO series, I have more ways to tackle different objects with one scanner.”
—— lionsartworld
“If I had to pick just one 3D scanner, I'd probably go with the MIRACO 2. I really like how it combines different scanning technologies in one device, letting me work on all kinds of projects without always needing a PC. And considering everything it can do, I honestly expected it to cost more!”
—— Luca Barsanti, FoxSource
"MIRACO 2 has performed really well in my scanning tests. Revopoint continues to improve its technology, and I’m impressed by how much this scanner can do. It allows me to scan objects of different sizes with great precision—even something as large as a car."
—— Tecniche Tornitura CNC
## Live Replay
MIRACO 2 made its debut at Formnext, drawing crowds eager to experience its standalone scanning power. Visitors explored its versatile scanning modes and watched detailed 3D results appear instantly on the built-in display.
## 6 Scanning Modes
MIRACO 2 combines blue multi-line laser scanning with near-infrared full-field and VCSEL structured light. Switch between six modes to capture intricate components, dark or reflective surfaces, deep holes, human bodies, and medium-to-large workpieces.
Rapidly scan black, reflective or metallic workpieces with 34 crossed blue laser lines and a data capture rate of up to 2.5 million points per second. It’s a powerful choice for efficient scanning across broader surfaces.
For objects with distinct texture or geometric features, marker-free laser scanning can also cut down on preparation time.
15 blue parallel laser lines balance fine-detail capture with efficient local coverage, making this mode well-suited to complex workpieces and close-range scanning.
Deep holes, narrow grooves, and recessed features can leave gaps in an otherwise complete model. MIRACO 2’s single-line mode helps you reach those difficult areas and fill in the details.
Capture dense point clouds with full-field infrared structured light. Use feature-based or marker-based alignment according to the object and scene. Continuous scanning, single-shot capture, and digital zoom give you more control over detailed projects.
Scan people and medium-to-large workpieces without markers using a high-density infrared dot pattern. In USB-connected PC mode, VCSEL scanning reaches up to 30 fps for smooth, efficient capture.
Combining Full-Field HD and VCSEL projection, Hybrid HD delivers detailed 3D capture with stable, reliable tracking. With a point return rate of up to 10 million points per second, it rapidly captures dense point clouds while maintaining smooth scanning continuity.
It's ideal for efficiently scanning people, medium-to-large workpieces, and complex surfaces where both fine detail and fast, stable tracking matter.
## Agent-Powered Ecosystem
Tired of complex CAD tools, manual scan cleanup, and incompatible software for design and inspection?
Powered by natural language commands, Revo Agents simplifies 3D workflows with automated point cloud fusion, Scan-to-CAD conversion, and Scan-to-Inspection analysis. Paired with MIRACO 2, it bridges high-precision scanning and production-ready results while reducing manual work.
Every backer receives 3 months of free Maker Plan trial credits. Unlock the Stretch Goal to get 1 additional free month.
MIRACO 2 delivers single-frame accuracy of up to 0.02 mm in multi-line laser mode, giving you a strong foundation for reverse engineering, part digitization, and dimensional workflows.
## From Small Components to Large Workpieces
With a recommended minimum scan size of 10 × 10 × 10 mm, the MIRACO 2 can capture small components, fittings, and intricate parts. For larger objects, pair it with the Photogrammetric Metrology Kit and a global marker workflow to extend the maximum scan volume to 5 × 5 × 5 m.
## What Our Beta Testers Say
## Photogrammetric Metrology
For larger objects, the Photogrammetric Metrology Kit* works with MIRACO 2’s dual RGB cameras, supporting 8K + 2K photogrammetry to improve global positioning accuracy, reduce cumulative error, and enable precise large-scale measurement. Advanced global marker algorithms calculate their positions, achieving photogrammetric length accuracy of 0.02 mm + 0.05 mm × L (m).
*The Photogrammetric Metrology Kit is sold separately in the Add-ons section.
## All-in-One Scanning
MIRACO 2 is built for the moments when the object can’t come to your desk. Its onboard computing platform handles depth calculation, 3D scanning, point cloud processing, photogrammetry, and basic editing. Use the 6-inch 2K AMOLED touchscreen to adjust settings, check coverage, and spot areas that need another pass.
At 960 g, MIRACO 2 is ready to move from the workshop to the job site without turning every scan into a full equipment setup.
MIRACO 2's built-in 10,000 mAh battery provides approximately 3 hours of runtime, so you can scan with fewer interruptions. With 65 W fast charging, it can reach 90% charge in less than one hour.
You can also add the Power Bank Kit from the Add-ons section for up to 3 additional hours of runtime.
## High-Speed Scanning
When connected to a PC via USB-C with NVIDIA GPU acceleration, MIRACO 2 reaches up to 120 fps in Multi-line Laser Mode. In PC mode, VCSEL scanning reaches up to 30 fps, while Full-field HD and Hybrid HD reach up to 15–25 fps, helping you capture large objects and complex scenes with a smoother scanning experience.
## Marker-Free Laser Scanning
MIRACO 2's cross-line and parallel-line laser modes support marker-free scanning* for objects with well-defined surface textures, distinct edges, or rich geometric features. Skip the preparation work and start capturing sooner, while preserving the fine details of the object.
*Marker-free scanning is supported in PC mode only.
## Outdoor Scanning
Scan outdoor equipment, public artworks, vehicle components, and on-site structures without waiting to bring them indoors. MIRACO 2 supports outdoor scanning in bright lighting conditions, with both VCSEL Rapid Scanning and Multi-line Laser Scanning supporting ambient illuminance of up to 100,000 lux.
MIRACO 2 pairs a 2 MP near-range RGB camera with a 50 MP RGB camera used for photogrammetry. Capture color alongside geometry for objects where appearance matters, from ceramics and artworks to props and cultural artifacts.
In PC mode, photo texturing adds another way to bring visual detail to your models.
## 3D Gaussian Splatting
In PC mode, MIRACO 2 converts point cloud and RGB scan data into photorealistic 1:1 Gaussian Splatting models. Export your results in .splat format for use in game development, animation, virtual reality, and other immersive content workflows.
## AI-Powered Targeting and Cropping
In PC mode, AI-powered object segmentation identifies your target with a single click and tracks it throughout the scan, helping remove irrelevant background point clouds and produce cleaner data. AI cropping also streamlines model processing.
In standalone mode, plane cropping is available, and AI cropping can be applied to color scans during post-processing.
## Free Scanning Software
MIRACO 2 helps you capture and refine scan data on the device, then continue more demanding work in Revo Scan 6 on your PC. Export common 3D formats for 3D printing, modeling, visualization, and downstream engineering workflows.
Supported output formats: PLY, OBJ, STL, ASC, 3MF, GLTF, FBX, Splat, STEP
Format availability and the steps needed to create a particular output may vary by workflow and software. For professional CAD design and inspection, MIRACO 2 can also work alongside Revopoint’s broader software ecosystem.
No more juggling software. With MIRACO 2, Revo Design, and Revo Measure, scanning, CAD, and inspection happen effortlessly in a single professional ecosystem.
## CAD Software
Featuring powerful tools for mesh editing, freeform and parametric modeling, and scan-to-CAD workflows, Revo Design* is perfect for reverse engineering, product development, and industrial design.
*Sold separately in the Add-ons section.
## Inspection Software
Transform your 3D scan data into accurate, verifiable measurements to ensure every part meets its design specifications. Powered by PTB-certified metrology algorithms, Revo Measure* delivers reliable, standards-based inspection for critical engineering and quality control workflows.
*Sold separately in the Add-ons section.
## Rewards
## Which MIRACO 2 Configuration Is Right for You?
Both configurations include the same accessories and scanning capabilities. The only difference is the RAM and storage capacity.
## MIRACO 2 16 GB + 256 GB
The Best Choice for Most Users
Handles most indoor and outdoor scanning tasks, from small objects to medium and large workpieces. Ideal for makers, designers, engineers, and users with diverse scanning needs.
## MIRACO 2 32 GB + 512 GB
For Large and Complex Projects
Designed for high-load scanning tasks involving vehicles, oversized objects, complex artifacts, or fossils. The extra RAM and storage let you capture longer projects and keep more scan data locally.
Not sure which to choose? The 16 GB + 256 GB configuration is enough for most scanning needs. Choose 32 GB + 512 GB for frequent, large-scale, or data-intensive projects.
## What’s in the Box
Both MIRACO 2 configurations include:
## Add-ons
## Applications
## Reverse Engineering
Capture legacy parts, complex surfaces, and hard-to-reach features before moving your scan data into a scan-to-CAD workflow.
## Industrial Inspection
Create detailed point clouds of components, tooling, castings, and production samples for downstream dimensional comparison and quality analysis.
## Automotive Projects
Digitize interior parts, body components, wheels, and custom-fit modifications. Use photogrammetric global references when a larger scan needs dimensional consistency.
## Molds and Tooling
Capture cavities, grooves, holes, and worn features to support repair, reproduction, and design updates.
## Cultural Heritage and Art
Record the shape and appearance of sculptures, ceramics, artifacts, and decorative works for documentation, restoration reference, or digital display.

Over the years, we’ve built, shipped, and supported 3D scanners used by creators, engineers, educators, and businesses around the world. With that experience behind us, we’re confident in our ability to deliver MIRACO 2 on schedule and to the quality our backers expect.

From high-precision scanning to CAD and inspection, MIRACO 2 puts a powerful 3D workflow in your hands. Work standalone when you’re on the move, connect to a PC for more demanding projects, and use Revo Agents in PC mode to turn natural-language instructions into streamlined workflows—from scan to CAD to inspection.

faq.q: How is MIRACO 2 different from the original MIRACO?
faq.a:
MIRACO 2 builds on the all-in-one design of the original MIRACO and adds a broader set of scanning capabilities, higher performance and new workflows.

• Higher accuracy: up to 0.02 mm single-frame accuracy(blue multi-line laser), compared with 0.05 mm(infrared structured light) for MIRACO.
• More scanning options: 34-line cross laser, 15-line parallel laser, single-line deep-hole laser, Full-field HD, VCSEL Rapid and Hybrid HD—giving you more options for different objects and surfaces.
• Better…

MIRACO 2 is designed for professionals and experienced makers who need a portable scanner for accurate work in the workshop, office or field. Common applications include:

• Industrial inspection and quality control
• Reverse engineering and product development
• Automotive parts, repair and customization
• Molds, tooling, jigs and fixtures
• Cultural heritage and artwork documentation
• Human and full-body scanning, including custom medical aids
• 3D printing and personalized products
• On-site…

faq.q: What size objects can MIRACO 2 scan?
faq.a: The recommended minimum scan size is 10 × 10 × 10 mm. With the Photogrammetric Metrology Kit and a global-marker workflow, MIRACO 2 can scan objects up to 5 × 5 × 5 m. That range covers small components, sculptures, vehicle sections and large equipment. Very small objects or smooth, featureless surfaces may require extra care and a suitable marker strategy.

faq.q: What kind of accuracy can I expect from MIRACO 2?
faq.a:
Accuracy depends on the scanning mode and setup. The specifications are:
• Multi-line Laser single-frame accuracy: up to 0.02 mm
• Full-field HD single-frame accuracy: 0.08 mm
• VCSEL structured-light accuracy: 0.10 mm at 300–500 mm; 0.20 mm at 500–700 mm; 0.30 mm at 800–1000 mm
• Laser volumetric accuracy: 0.02 mm + 0.05 mm × L (m), where L is the object length
• Photogrammetric accuracy with the Metrology Kit: 0.02 mm + 0.05 mm × L (m), where L is the maximum measurement distance
• Minimum poi…

faq.q: What are MIRACO 2’s working distances and capture areas?
faq.a:
Working distance
• Multi-line Laser: 200–500 mm
• Full-field HD and Hybrid HD: 200–600 mm
• VCSEL: 300–1000 mm

Single-capture area
• 137 × 138 mm at 200 mm
• 411 × 345 mm at 500 mm in Multi-line Laser Mode
• 467 × 414 mm at 600 mm in Full-field HD and Hybrid HD Modes
• 692 × 690 mm at 1000 mm in VCSEL Mode

Frame rate depends on the scanning mode and whether you scan standalone or through a PC.
Standalone mode
• Multi-line Laser: up to 50 fps
• Full-field HD and Hybrid HD: 13-15 fps
• VCSEL: 13-15 fps

PC mode
• Multi-line Laser: 80–120 fps with an NVIDIA GPU, or 40–60 fps using the CPU
• Full-field HD and Hybrid HD: 15–25 fps
• VCSEL: 20–30 fps
Point capture rate: up to 2.5 million points per second in Multi-line Laser Mode and up to 10 million points per second in Hybrid HD Mode.

faq.q: Can I scan outdoors or in bright light?
faq.a: Yes. MIRACO 2 supports ambient illuminance up to 100,000 lux in VCSEL Mode and Multi-line Laser Mode. For the best results, avoid strong direct sunlight on the object whenever possible, especially when scanning reflective surfaces.

faq.q: Can MIRACO 2 scan black, metallic, reflective or transparent objects?
faq.a:
MIRACO 2 is designed to handle many challenging surfaces.
• Black or dark objects: supported.
• Metallic and highly reflective objects: supported in Multi-line Laser Modes, usually without surface treatment.
• Transparent or mirror-like objects: apply a 3D scanning spray or developer spray before scanning. These surfaces remain difficult for most optical scanners without treatment.

faq.q: Can I scan large or featureless objects without markers?
faq.a:
Sometimes. Marker-free scanning works best when an object has clear texture, distinctive geometry or recognizable edges. MIRACO 2 also supports color alignment in the laser line mode, which can help when the object has visible patterns or color variation.
If the surface is smooth, plain or repetitive, tracking may be unreliable without markers. For the most reliable results—especially on large objects—use markers. For large-object accuracy, use the global-marker workflow with the Photogrammetric…

Yes. For large objects such as a car, use the Photogrammetric Metrology Kit to establish a global coordinate frame, then capture the surface with a laser scanning mode. This workflow helps control accumulated alignment error across large areas. A car scan will take time to set up, capture and process, so plan your marker placement and post-processing before you begin.

faq.q: What scanning modes does MIRACO 2 offer?
faq.a:
MIRACO 2 combines blue multi-line laser, near-infrared full-field structured light and VCSEL near-infrared structured light in six scanning modes:

• 34-Line Blue Cross Laser: for high-accuracy scanning, including dark, metallic and reflective surfaces. Marker-free scanning is possible on objects with sufficient texture or geometric detail in PC mode only.
• 15-Line Blue Parallel Laser: balances detail and coverage for close-range scanning of complex parts.

faq.q: Which scanning mode should I use?
faq.a:
• Cross laser: choose it for precision work, including dark, metallic or reflective surfaces.
• Parallel laser: a versatile option for detailed, close-range scans of complex parts.
• Single-line deep-hole: use it to capture narrow or recessed features such as holes and grooves.
• Full-field HD: use it when you need detailed point clouds and the object has enough features for reliable tracking.
